items.title: One threat actor responsible for 83% of recent Ivanti RCE attacks
items.description: Threat intelligence observations show that a single threat actor is responsible for most of the active exploitation of two critical vulnerabilities in Ivanti Endpoint Manager Mobile (EPMM), tracked as CVE-2026-21962 and CVE-2026-24061. [...]

items.title: Snail mail letters target Trezor and Ledger users in crypto-theft attacks
items.description: Threat actors are sending physical letters pretending to be from Trezor and Ledger, makers of cryptocurrency hardware wallets, to trick users into submitting recovery phrases in crypto theft attacks. [...]

items.title: Over 300 Malicious Chrome Extensions Caught Leaking or Stealing User Data
items.description: With more than 37 million combined downloads, the extensions expose users to tracking and personal information theft. The post Over 300 Malicious Chrome Extensions Caught Leaking or Stealing User Data appeared first on SecurityWeek.

items.title: New Clickfix Attack Uses DNS Hijacking to Spread Malware
items.description: A new evolution in the ClickFix social engineering campaign, which now employs a custom DNS hijacking technique to deliver malware. This attack method tricks users into executing malicious commands that utilize DNS lookups to fetch the next stage of the infection, allowing attackers to bypass traditional detection methods and blend in with normal network traffic. items.title: Threat Actors Exploit Claude Artifacts and Google Ads to Target macOS Users
items.description: A sophisticated malware campaign targeting macOS users through Google-sponsored search results and legitimate platforms, including Anthropic’s Claude AI and Medium. items.title: Threat Actor Allegedly Selling Critical Severity OpenSea 0-day Exploit Chain on Hacking Forums
items.description: A threat actor is reportedly selling a purported critical severity zero-day exploit chain targeting OpenSea for $100,000 USD in Bitcoin or Monero. The listing claims the vulnerability remains unpatched and undisclosed, raising alarms in the NFT community. items.title: CISA Warns of Microsoft Configuration Manager SQL Injection Vulnerability Exploited in Attacks
items.description: CISA has issued an urgent alert about a critical SQL injection vulnerability in Microsoft Configuration Manager (SCCM). Tracked as CVE-2024-43468, this flaw lets unauthenticated attackers run malicious commands on servers and databases.
